title: Iberian Union
capsule: The Iberian Union was the dynastic personal union of the Portuguese and Spanish crowns under the Habsburg dynasty, formally ratified at the Cortes of Tomar in 1581 following Philip II of Spain's military victory over Portuguese pretenders at the Battle of Alcântara in 1580, triggered by the extinction of the House of Aviz after King Sebastian's death at the Battle of Alcácer Quibir in 1578. The union incorporated the entire Iberian Peninsula and combined two of the world's largest colonial empires, spanning the Americas, Africa, India, and Southeast Asia, though Portugal and Spain maintained separate administrations, laws, and overseas possessions. Philip IV's financial demands and mismanagement of the Catalan Revolt (1640) provoked Portuguese nobles to launch the Restauração on 1 December 1640, installing the Duke of Braganza as John IV of Portugal. Spain did not formally recognise Portuguese independence until the Treaty of Lisbon in 1668.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Iberian Peninsula's core extent is unambiguous; colonial holdings are historically documented but the precise governance boundaries between the two crowns' overseas territories were often blurred in practice.
